QuestionText: If a vertical mirror is placed to the right of the word 'TOY', what will the mirror image look like?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: A vertical mirror flips the left and right positions of the letters. The last letter 'Y' comes to the front, 'O' remains in the middle, and 'T' goes to the end, forming 'YOT'.

QuestionText: Which of the following capital letters looks exactly the same when viewed in a standard vertical mirror?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: The letter 'A' is perfectly symmetrical down its middle vertical line, so its left-to-right mirror reflection looks identical to the original letter.

QuestionText: A square sheet of paper is folded in half from left to right. A single small hole is punched right through the middle of the folded paper. When the paper is completely unfolded, how many holes will you see?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: Since the paper has 2 overlapping layers after being folded once, punching 1 hole through it creates 2 holes when unfolded.

QuestionText: If you look at the reflection of the capital letter 'E' in a water surface below it, what does its water image look like?
Options: A) It flips upside down but looks exactly like 'E'
C) It turns upside down and points left
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: A water reflection flips an object upside down (vertically). Because the letter 'E' is horizontally symmetrical across its middle, flipping it vertically does not change its appearance.

QuestionText: If the word 'MOM' is reflected in a vertical mirror on its right side, what word will appear in the reflection?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: Reversing the letter order of 'MOM' from right to left gives 'MOM'. Since both 'M' and 'O' are symmetrical, the image remains perfectly unchanged as 'MOM'.

QuestionText: A square piece of paper is folded in half from bottom to top. Then it is folded in half again from left to right. A hole is punched in the center of this smaller folded square. How many holes are visible when it is unfolded?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: Folding the paper twice creates 4 layers. Punching a hole through all 4 layers creates exactly 4 holes distributed across the fully opened sheet.

QuestionText: What does the water image of the number '8' look like?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: The number '8' is vertically symmetrical (the top half mirrors the bottom half), so flipping it upside down keeps it looking like an '8'.

QuestionText: If a vertical mirror is placed to the right of the word 'BOX', what string will you see in the mirror?
Options: D) X, a backward O, and a backward B
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: The order of letters reverses to X-O-B, and each individual letter is flipped horizontally. While 'X' and 'O' look the same, 'B' turns around backward. Thus, it looks like X, O, and a backward B.

QuestionText: Which of these shapes will change its appearance completely when looked at in a water image reflection?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: A water reflection flips objects upside down. An upward-pointing triangle (▲) will turn around completely to point downward (▼).

QuestionText: A square piece of paper is folded along its diagonal line to form a triangle. A single cut is made to snip off the sharp top corner point. When unfolded, what will the cut area in the middle of the paper look like?
Options: A) A diamond or square cutout
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: Cutting a corner along a diagonal fold line creates a symmetrical four-sided diamond or square cutout right in the center of the opened paper.

QuestionText: If you hold a clock up to a vertical mirror and the reflection shows the hands pointing straight up to 12 and straight down to 6, what actual time is the clock showing?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: When a clock reads 6:00, the hands form a straight vertical line. A vertical mirror reflection does not change perfectly vertical lines, so the time remains 6:00.

QuestionText: Which letter does NOT change its shape in both a vertical mirror reflection AND a water image reflection?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: The letter 'H' has both a vertical line of symmetry and a horizontal line of symmetry, meaning it stays completely identical in both kinds of reflections.

QuestionText: If you write the number '1' on a paper and hold it up to a mirror, the mirror image will show the top small hook pointing in which direction if it originally pointed left?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: A vertical mirror reverses left and right, so a small hook pointing to the left will appear to point to the right in the reflection.

QuestionText: A strip of paper is folded into three equal overlapping layers (Z-fold). A heart shape is punched through the folded stack. When unfolded, how many hearts will appear in a row?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: Three overlapping layers mean the hole punch pierces 3 individual panels, creating a row of 3 heart-shaped cutouts upon unfolding.

QuestionText: What happens to the word 'CODE' when it is viewed as a water image?
Options: A) It reads upside down but the letters still spell C-O-D-E cleanly
B) It reads backward as E-D-O-C
C) It flips completely upside down and backward
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: All letters in the word 'CODE' (C, O, D, E) are horizontally symmetrical. When flipped vertically in a water image, they look exactly like themselves, keeping the spelling intact.

QuestionText: Which of these numbers looks exactly the same when flipped upside down in water?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: The number '0' is symmetrical horizontally, so flipping it vertically in a water image leaves its appearance completely unchanged.

QuestionText: If you raise your right hand in front of a flat dressing mirror, which hand does your reflection appear to raise?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: A mirror causes lateral inversion, turning left into right and right into left. Raising your right hand makes your reflection raise its left hand.

QuestionText: A square paper is folded in half from left to right. Then a small triangle is cut out along the crease line (the fold edge). What will the cutout look like when opened?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: Cutting a triangle out of a folded crease line mirrors the triangle to the other side when opened, joining the bases to form a four-sided diamond shape.

QuestionText: If you look at an arrow pointing to the right (➔) in a mirror placed on its right, which way does the arrow in the reflection point?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: The arrow points toward the mirror surface, so its reflection will also point back toward the mirror surface, which means it points left.

QuestionText: Which capital letter looks different in a mirror but stays the same in a water image reflection?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: The letter 'K' changes when reflected horizontally in a mirror (points turn left), but stays identical when flipped vertically in water because its top and bottom halves match.

QuestionText: If you fold a paper in half and punch 3 separate holes along the loose open edges (not on the fold), how many holes show up when you unfold it?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: Since the paper is folded into 2 layers, punching 3 holes through both layers yields a total of 3 × 2 = 6 holes when opened.

QuestionText: What does the letter 'V' look like when reflected in a water image?
Options: B) A letter that looks like '^'
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: Flipping the letter 'V' upside down turns its open top downward and its sharp point upward, making it look like a caret or an inverted 'A' shape (^).

QuestionText: If a word in a mirror reads exactly as 'RAT' from left to right, what was the original word written on the card?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: To get 'RAT' in the mirror, the original card must be written backward starting with a backward T, a normal A, and a backward R. Reading it normally spells TAR.

QuestionText: A square paper sheet is folded from top to bottom. A tiny square is cut out from the bottom open edge. What does the cutout look like when opened?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: Because the cut is made on the open edges (not on the folded crease), the cut doesn't mirror across a fold line; it creates two separate independent square cutouts.

QuestionText: Which letter will look backwards when viewed in a side mirror, but perfectly fine when viewed upside down in water?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: The letter 'B' turns backward in a mirror, but its top and bottom halves are symmetrical, so its water reflection looks completely normal.

QuestionText: If you hold a paper with the word 'OH' written on it in front of a mirror, what does the text look like in the reflection?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: The letters reverse positions from left-to-right, so 'O' goes to the back and 'H' comes to the front. Since both letters are symmetrical, it reads clearly as 'HO'.

QuestionText: A round circular filter paper is folded exactly in half to make a semi-circle. It is folded in half once more into a wedge shape. A small notch is cut into the curved edge. When fully opened, how many notches will be on the circle?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: Folding a circle in half and in half again creates 4 overlapping layers. A single cut into the edge leaves 4 evenly spaced notches around the perimeter of the circle.

QuestionText: Which of these punctuation marks looks exactly the same in a vertical mirror reflection?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: An exclamation mark (!) consists of a vertical line and a centered dot. It is perfectly symmetrical from left to right, so its mirror image does not change.

QuestionText: If you look at a drawing of a boat floating on a river, the water image of the boat's tall mast pole will point in which direction?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: Water reflections invert objects vertically. A mast pole pointing straight up above the water line will appear to point straight down beneath the surface line.

QuestionText: A square paper is folded along both diagonal lines into a small triangle layout. If a single hole is punched directly through the center point where all folds cross, how many holes show up when opened?
SubTopic: Mirrors, Water Images, and Paper Folding
Explanation: Because the punch is made exactly on the central shared intersection point of all folds, the hole stays positioned in the dead center without replicating across panels. You will only see 1 single hole.
